title: Compliance delivery: APIs + webhooks for audit/retention/residency events
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: implement a first-class Compliance Events API and webhook delivery system that emits auditable events and evidence bundles for data residency, retention, and deletion lifecycle actions. This ticket covers API endpoints, webhook schema + signing, storage of signed evidence for audits, reporting exports, and operational controls (retries, DLQ, backpressure). The design must satisfy legal and SOC/ISO auditors: proof of residency changes, retention policy enforcement, deletion confirmations, and automated report generation. Scope excludes UI console wireframes (separate PM/Design tickets) but includes API contract and backend plumbing for event generation and delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Public REST API endpoints exposed for: event query (by tenant, time range), manual evidence export, and retention policy status checks.

Webhook delivery system emits events for: residency_change, retention_policy_applied, data_deletion_confirmed, retention_overrides, audit_log_entry. Events are HMAC-signed and versioned (v1) with idempotency keys.
Evidence bundles (signed JSON + server-side signature) are stored for a minimum of 7 years for flagged customers and accessible via API for authorized auditor principals.
System supports at-least-once delivery semantics with DLQ and exponential backoff; webhook delivery guarantees documented and tested.
APIs require tenant-scoped RBAC and OIDC-based service principals; KMS integration for signing evidence is validated in staging.
Automated nightly reporting job aggregates residency & retention events into a tenant-level CSV and stores S3 URI accessible via API.
End-to-end integration tests exist covering event emit -> webhook delivery -> evidence storage -> auditor export.
PM and Legal sign-off on event schemas and retention durations recorded in ticket comments.
tasks: Spike: event schema options and legal review (done)
Implement event producer hooks in runtime for retention/residency actions
Build Compliance Events API: GET /v1/compliance/events, POST /v1/compliance/export
Webhook delivery engine: signing, retries, DLQ, idempotency
Evidence store: signed bundles, index by tenant/event type/date
KMS integration for signing evidence bundles
Security review and threat model update
Add end-to-end integration tests and load tests for webhook throughput
Docs: API spec, webhook verification guide, runbook for DLQ recovery
decisions: Event bus: use existing internal event-broker (Kafka) with a dedicated compliance topic to preserve ordering per-tenant
Evidence signing: use envelope signing via KMS (asymmetric) to produce tamper-evident bundles
Residency enforcement: record authoritative region at object creation time and emit residency_change events when rehost/migration occurs
Retention TTL enforcement: combine scheduled background sweeper + synchronous confirmation event when deletion completes
Webhook semantics: at-least-once delivery with HMAC-SHA256 signature header and x-compliance-event-id for dedupe
technical_notes: Event schema v1 drafted in docs link; minimal fields: event_id, tenant_id, type, occurred_at, resource_list, evidence_uri, signature_metadata
Include sequence_number per-tenant to help auditors and reconciliation jobs
Store evidence bundles in customer-scoped S3 with server-side encryption and retention at object metadata level
Design for multi-region writes: primary region writes canonical event then fanout to residency-region replicas
Rate limits: per-tenant webhook cap of 1000/s and burst 5000 with queueing; evaluate for Dedicated customers separately
Expose webhook subscription admin APIs for customers to register endpoints and provide verification token
Audit trail retention: default 5 years; allow enterprise override to 7 years via contract flag
Observability: add per-event latency histograms, webhook success/failure counters, and DLQ size gauges

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Missed events during region migration could break residency audit. Mitigation: tombstone + reconciliation job comparing storage location vs events; add sequence numbers per tenant.
Risk: Webhook endpoints may be unreliable causing backpressure. Mitigation: DLQ, per-tenant circuit breaker, and an admin console to replay failed events
Risk: Evidence access may expose PII. Mitigation: enforce tenant-scoped authorization, presigned URLs with short TTL, and audit access logs
